005package org.wpilib.annotation;
006
007import java.lang.annotation.ElementType;
008import java.lang.annotation.Retention;
009import java.lang.annotation.RetentionPolicy;
010import java.lang.annotation.Target;
011
012/**
013 * Marks a method as a post-construction initializer. The WPILib compiler plugin will check for uses
014 * of methods with this annotation and report a compiler error if the method is not called after the
015 * object is constructed.
016 *
017 * <p>Limitations of this annotation:
018 *
019 * <ul>
020 *   <li>Initializer methods must be called on the variable directly. They cannot be detected if
021 *       called indirectly (e.g., on an object returned by a method)
022 *       <pre>{@code
023 * // This is OK
024 * Foo foo = new Foo();
025 * foo.init();
026 *
027 * // This is not OK
028 * Box box = new Box(new Foo());
029 * box.getFoo().init();
030 *
031 * }</pre>
032 *   <li>Static initializer methods must accept exactly one parameter of the type that defines the
033 *       static method (they cannot accept a parameter of a supertype or derived type).
034 *   <li>Static initializer methods with multiple parameters of the initialized type must annotate
035 *       one of them with {@link InitializedParam} to disambiguate for the compiler.
036 * </ul>
037 *
038 * <p>Errors reported by the compiler plugin may be suppressed by annotating the offending method
039 * with {@code SuppressWarnings("PostConstructionInitializer")} or {@code
040 * SuppressWarnings(PostConstructionInitializer.SUPPRESSION_KEY)}. This is intended to be used in
041 * tests to allow runtime error handling code to be tested, but may also be used to suppress
042 * spurious warnings in production code.
043 */
044@Target(ElementType.METHOD)
045@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)
046public @interface PostConstructionInitializer {
047  /**
048   * The string key to use in {@link SuppressWarnings} annotations to suppress compiler error
049   * messages related to this annotation.
050   */
051  String SUPPRESSION_KEY = "PostConstructionInitializer";
052
053  /**
054   * Marks a specific parameter in a static initializer method as being the initialized object. This
055   * disambiguates situations where static initializer methods accept multiple arguments of the same
056   * initialize-required type; for example:
057   *
058   * <pre>{@code
059   * class Foo {
060   *   @PostConstructionInitializer
061   *   static void copy(Foo src, @InitializedParam Foo dst) {
062   *     // ...
063   *   }
064   * }
065   * }</pre>
066   *
067   * <p>Static initializer methods must have a parameter of the exact type that defines the static
068   * method.
069   *
070   * <pre>{@code
071   * interface I {
072   *   @PostConstructionInitializer
073   *   static void init(I object) { ... }
074   * }
075   *
076   * class Foo implements I {
077   *   @PostConstructionInitializer
078   *   static void initFoo(Foo foo) { ... } // OK
079   *
080   *   @PostConstructionInitializer
081   *   static void initI(I object) { ... } // ERROR: I is not Foo
082   *
083   *   @PostConstructionInitializer
084   *   static void initOther(SomeOtherType o) { ... } // ERROR: SomeOtherType is not Foo
085   * }
086   * }</pre>
087   */
088  @Target(ElementType.PARAMETER)
089  @Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)
090  @interface InitializedParam {}
091}
